sources.entry: 🧰 Resilience engineering papers: comprehensive list of resources on resilience engineering

summary.one_liner: A curated, annotated reading list of resilience engineering papers, organized by researcher, with notes on key concepts and related fields such as cognitive systems engineering.
summary.what_it_does: This is a Markdown reading guide rather than software. It has an overview, pointers to two annotation sources (Ben Hutchinson's safety summaries and Thai Wood's Resilience Roundup), and a long alphabetical list of people active in resilience engineering and adjacent fields. Each person entry lists concepts they write about and selected publications, talks, or books. It also covers "big ideas" such as Safety-I/Safety-II, ETTO, drift into failure, STAMP, and robust yet fragile systems, with short summaries of several of them. The README is truncated, so the later part of the list is not visible here. The publication lists are described by the author as partial, covering only papers the author has read or queued.
use_cases: Finding foundational resilience engineering papers to read
Learning who the key researchers in resilience engineering are
Looking up concepts like Safety-II, ETTO, or drift into failure
Starting a study of human factors in incident analysis
Finding summaries of safety and incident research
notable: Organized by researcher, with the concepts each person is associated with
Covers the Safety-I vs Safety-II framing and Hollnagel's FRAM and ETTO principle
Includes summaries of Dekker's drift into failure and just culture ideas
Links to external annotation sources (Ben Hutchinson's blog, Thai Wood's Resilience Roundup)
Points to a 'where do I start' guide and a Zotero group of the linked papers
caveats: Publication lists are partial by the author's own statement, covering only what they have read or queued
The README is truncated, so the full list of people is not visible
Many links in the list are bare references with no target URL shown
keywords: work as imagined vs work as done
